Circle()
    .drawOn()
    .frame(width: 80, height: 80)

SignaturePath()
    .drawOn(isDrawn: signed, style: .blue, lineWidth: 3, duration: 1.6)

effects.name: Progress Ring
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI ProgressRing (iOS 17+) with progress (0…1), lineWidth (12 pt), colors (cyan, blue, purple) and an optional label view builder (default: the percentage). In a ZStack, stroke a full Circle in secondary at 18 % opacity, then a Circle().trim(from: 0, to: progress) stroked with AngularGradient(colors:) over 0–360° and a round line cap, rotated −90° so it starts at twelve o'clock. Pad by lineWidth / 2. Animate progress changes with .spring(response: 0.6, dampingFraction: 0.75). The default label is the percentage as .title2.bold().monospacedDigit() with .contentTransition(.numericText(value:)), so the digits roll. Expose the percentage as the accessibility value. With Reduce Motion on, use a short ease.
effects.summary: A gradient ring springs to each value as the percentage rolls.

effects.name: Skeleton
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .skeleton(isLoading:) view modifier (iOS 17+). While loading, apply .redacted(reason: .placeholder) so text and images become grey blocks in the view's real layout, then the shimmer modifier (a white 80 % highlight band, 35 % of the width, sweeping left to right every 1.6 s, masked by the content), disable hit testing and hide the view from accessibility. When loading ends, remove both and animate with easeInOut(0.3 s) so the real content fades in. The shimmer pauses for Reduce Motion.
effects.summary: A shimmering placeholder of the view's own layout while it loads.

effects.name: Sliding Tabs
effects.prompt: Create a generic SwiftUI SlidingTabs control (iOS 17+) over Hashable options with a selection binding, an indicator style (.pill or .underline), a tint and a title closure (plus a convenience init for [String]). Show the options as plain Buttons in an HStack inside a 4 pt padded capsule tinted secondary at 12 % (pill style only). Behind the selected title only, draw the indicator — a capsule filled with the tint (title turns white), or a 3 pt capsule at the bottom inset 10 pt (title turns tint) — with .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "indicator", in: namespace), so it glides between options. Change the selection inside withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.8)), and add the .isSelected trait. With Reduce Motion on, use a 0.15 s ease.
effects.summary: A segmented control whose pill or underline glides to the selection.

effects.name: Reading Progress
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI ReadingProgressScrollView(color:height:content:) (iOS 17+): a vertical ScrollView whose content gets a top overlay holding a Color.clear layer with a Capsule (4 pt tall, the colour, a soft glow shadow) at its top-leading edge. Drive the layer with visualEffect, not state or a PreferenceKey (preferences don't reliably leave an iOS scroll view): frame = proxy.frame(in: .scrollView), viewport = proxy.bounds(of: .scrollView)?.size, progress = clamp(−frame.minY / (frame.height − viewport.height), 0, 1); scaleEffect(x: viewport.width × progress / frame.width, anchor: .topLeading), then offset(x: −frame.minX, y: −frame.minY) to pin it to the top. Disable hit testing.
effects.summary: A bar along the top fills as you scroll through the content.

effects.name: Aurora
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI AuroraBackground view (iOS 17+). On a dark base color, draw one large circle per palette color (default purple, blue, teal, pink; 80% opacity, diameter 70% of the larger side). Each circle drifts on its own Lissajous path, x = cos(t·0.6 + phase)·30% width and y = sin(t·0.8 + phase·1.3)·30% height, where phase differs per index. Drive time from TimelineView(.animation) scaled by a speed parameter, blur the whole group with a ~60 pt radius, clip to bounds and hide it from accessibility.
effects.summary: Soft, blurred colour blobs drift slowly behind your content.

effects.name: Mesh Gradient
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI AnimatedMeshGradient view for iOS 18+ (mark it @available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)) with nine colours (indigo, purple, pink / blue, purple, orange / teal, mint, yellow by default; fewer are repeated) and a speed. Inside TimelineView(.animation), draw MeshGradient(width: 3, height: 3, points:colors:). Keep the four corners fixed; slide the four edge midpoints along their own edge by sin(t × 2π / period + offset) × 0.2, and move the centre point in both axes by 0.25, giving each a different period between 6 and 10 s so the motion never repeats visibly. Hide it from accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, pause it.
effects.summary: A 3×3 MeshGradient whose points drift so the colours flow like liquid.

effects.name: Retro Grid
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI RetroGrid view (iOS 17+) with color (pink), spacing (40 pt), speed (0.8 rows per second) and horizon (0.35 of the height). In a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation): with top = height × horizon and depth = height − top, draw horizontal lines at y = top + depth / z for z = n + 1 − fract(time × speed), n = 0…39, so the bottom edge is z = 1, rows bunch up toward the horizon and every row moves toward the viewer; draw lines from the vanishing point (centre, top) to (centre + k × spacing, bottom) for enough k to cover the width. Stroke the path twice: 3 pt at 35 % opacity for a glow, then 1 pt solid. Mask the view with a vertical gradient that is clear down to the horizon and opaque 45 % lower, so lines fade into the distance. Hide from accessibility; Reduce Motion pauses it.
effects.summary: A synthwave floor: a perspective grid scrolling toward you.

effects.name: Border Beam
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .borderBeam(cornerRadius:colors:lineWidth:length:duration:) view modifier (iOS 17+). In an overlay TimelineView(.animation), compute head = fract(time / duration) (4 s per lap). Stroke RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:, style: .continuous).trim(from: head − length, to: head) with a LinearGradient of the colours (orange, pink, purple), lineWidth 2 pt and round caps; when head − length is negative, also stroke trim(from: 1 + head − length, to: 1) so the beam wraps past the path's start seamlessly. Draw the beam twice, once blurred by 2 × lineWidth underneath for a glow. Pad by lineWidth / 2, disable hit testing and hide from accessibility. With Reduce Motion on, park the beam.
effects.summary: A short comet of light runs around the card's border forever.

effects.name: Waves
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI WaveBackground view (iOS 17+) with colors (one per layer, back to front: cyan 35 %, blue 45 %, indigo 70 %), amplitude (12 pt) and speed. In a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), for each layer with depth d = layer / (count − 1): baseline at height × (0.45 + 0.2 d), wavelength width × (0.9 − 0.3 d), phase = time × (0.6 + 0.5 d), alternating direction per layer. Build a path from the bottom-left corner along y = baseline + sin(x / wavelength × 2π + phase + layer) × amplitude × (0.7 + 0.3 d) sampled every 4 pt, down to the bottom-right corner, close it and fill it with the layer's colour. Hide from accessibility; Reduce Motion pauses it.
effects.summary: Layered sine waves roll across the bottom, back layers slower and paler.

effects.name: Film Grain
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .grain(opacity:isAnimated:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Generate a 128 × 128 grey noise CGImage once (8-bit DeviceGray, random bytes from a seeded generator, no interpolation). In an overlay, show it with Image(decorative:scale: 2).resizable(resizingMode: .tile) in a frame 64 pt larger than the view in each direction, clipped, and shift it by a different offset (frame × 37 mod 64, frame × 53 mod 64) 12 times a second using TimelineView(.periodic(by: 1/12)), so the grain flickers like film. Use .blendMode(.overlay) at opacity (0.35), disable hit testing and hide it from accessibility. With Reduce Motion on (or isAnimated false), keep the grain still.
effects.summary: Flickering film grain over any view, from a tiled noise texture.
effects.usage:
LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
    .grain()

HeroImage()
    .grain(opacity: 0.2, isAnimated: false)

effects.name: Flashlight
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .flashlight(radius:darkness:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Track the pointer with .onContinuousHover(coordinateSpace: .local) and a finger with a simultaneous DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0), storing the location in @State (nil on exit) plus the last location. In an overlay GeometryReader, draw a RadialGradient from clear to black at darkness (0.85) opacity, centred on the location as a UnitPoint, from startRadius 0.55 × radius to endRadius radius (90 pt), so everything outside the circle is dark with a soft edge. Fade the whole overlay out when the pointer leaves (lights back on) with easeOut(0.4 s), and follow the pointer with .interactiveSpring(response: 0.18). Disable hit testing. With Reduce Motion on, move without animation.
effects.summary: The view goes dark except a soft circle of light around the pointer.

effects.name: Lava Lamp
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI LavaLamp(colors:background:blobs:speed:) view (iOS 17+). In TimelineView(.animation), fill a vertical LinearGradient of the colours, masked by a Canvas that adds .alphaThreshold(min: 0.5, color: .black) then .blur(radius: 7 % of the smaller side), and in drawLayer fills 7 black ellipses: blob i (seed = i × 1.618) at x = width × (0.2 + 0.6 × (0.5 + 0.5 sin(seed × 3.1 + t × 0.13))), y = height × (0.5 + 0.48 sin(t × (0.18 + 0.05 × (i % 3)) + seed × 2.3)), radius = min side × (0.11 + 0.07 × (0.5 + 0.5 sin(seed × 5.7))), stretched vertically by 1 + 0.25 |cos(t × 0.2 + seed × 2.3)|, plus wide pools of wax at the bottom and top. The threshold fuses the blurred blobs into liquid shapes (metaballs). Put the background colour (deep purple) behind. With Reduce Motion on, show one still frame.
effects.summary: Soft blobs drift up and down, stretching and merging like hot wax.

effects.name: Matrix Rain
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI MatrixRain(color:fontSize:speed:) view (iOS 17+) drawn in a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Resolve every glyph (half-width katakana plus digits, monospaced, 14 pt) once per frame in the trail colour and in white. Columns are fontSize × 0.9 wide, rows fontSize × 1.1 tall. For each column, a stable random seed sets the trail length (8–22), the speed (6–16 rows/s) and a phase; the head row = (time × speed + seed × 97) mod (rows + length). Draw the head white at full opacity and each trail cell below it with opacity 0.85 × (1 − offset / length), picking the glyph from a hash of (column, row, floor(time × (2 + seed × 4))) so characters flicker. With Reduce Motion on, show one still frame.
effects.summary: Columns of glyphs rain down with bright heads and fading trails.

effects.name: Interactive Dot Grid
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI InteractiveDotGrid(spacing:color:highlight:radius:) view (iOS 17+). Track the pointer from a DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) and onContinuousHover (nil when released). In a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), smooth the pointer and a 0…1 strength each frame with exponential easing (k = 1 − e^(−14 dt) while active, strength decays with e^(−6 dt) after release) in a plain reference-type model. Draw a centred grid of dots every spacing points (18 pt): within radius (70 pt) of the pointer, near = (1 − d / radius)² × strength; push the dot away by near × spacing × 1.6, grow it by 2 × near and tint it with the highlight colour above 0.15. At rest, a faint wave sin((column + row) × 0.45 − time × 2) varies the radius by 0.5 pt. With Reduce Motion on, keep the highlight but don't move dots or run the wave.
effects.summary: A grid of dots scatters away from your finger and eases back.

effects.name: Meteors
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI Meteors(count:angle:color:showsStars:) view (iOS 17+) drawn in a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Scatter 60 faint static stars (0.4–1.2 pt, 25–65 % opacity) from a stable hash. Each meteor i has a flight time of 1.6–3.8 s and a pause of 0.5–3 s; when in flight, its head moves from a start point spread along the top edge and the side it comes from along the direction (angle 135° in y-down coordinates, so they travel down and to the left) by (width + height) × 1.2 × progress. Stroke its 50–110 pt tail from the tail point to the head with a linear gradient clear → 90 % colour, 1.5 pt wide, round caps, and draw a 5 pt head with a 2 pt blur. With Reduce Motion on, draw the stars only.
effects.summary: Meteors streak across a starry sky with glowing heads and fading tails.

effects.name: Flow Field
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI FlowField(lines:colors:speed:) view (iOS 17+) drawn in a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Define a flow angle field(x, y, t) = (sin(x × 0.012 + t) × cos(y × 0.014 − 0.7t) + sin((x + y) × 0.007 + 0.5t)) × π, with coordinates scaled so the smaller side maps to about 220 units and t = time × 0.25. For each of 140 lines, start at a stable random point and integrate 22 steps of 3.2 pt along the field into a Path. Stroke it in a colour picked from the list at 18 % opacity, then again at 85 % with a dash [5, 40] and dashPhase −((time × 30 + random × 45) mod 45), so short dashes travel along the curves (wrap the phase: a huge dash phase makes Core Graphics hang). With Reduce Motion on, show one still frame.
effects.summary: Generative curves follow a shifting vector field with dashes flowing along them.

effects.name: Rolling Number
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI RollingNumber view (iOS 17+) that displays a number with odometer-style digit rolling. Render Text(value, format:) with monospacedDigit(), apply .contentTransition(.numericText(value:)) so digits roll up when the value increases and down when it decreases, and animate changes with .snappy. Provide initialisers for Int and for Double with a FloatingPointFormatStyle.
effects.summary: Digits roll like an odometer when the value changes.

effects.name: Split-Flap Display
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI SplitFlapText(_ text:size:tile:ink:) view (iOS 17+), upper-casing the text, with one flap cell per character in an HStack. Each cell is size × 0.78 wide and size × 1.3 tall (size 36), drawn from four halves of a monospaced bold character on a rounded dark tile, each half clipped to the top or bottom half: static top = next character, static bottom = current, a top flap showing current rotated with rotation3DEffect about the x axis anchored at .bottom, and a bottom flap showing next anchored at .top; a thin dark line covers the seam. When the target changes, after a 0.05 s × index delay, step through the characters of the board alphabet " A…Z0…9:.-/" from current towards the target (at most the last 6 steps); each step folds the top flap 0 → −90° (.easeIn, 0.07 s), then the bottom flap 90° → 0 (.easeOut, 0.07 s), then commits next as current and resets the angles without animation. With Reduce Motion on, change instantly.
effects.summary: Characters flip through the alphabet like an airport departures board.

effects.name: Slot Machine
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI SlotMachineNumber(value:digits:size:) view (iOS 17+) that zero-pads the value and shows one reel per digit. A reel is a VStack of 40 rows (row % 10, heavy rounded monospaced digits, size × 1.25 tall) offset by −index × rowHeight and clipped to one row, on a rounded secondary-12 % tile with a top/bottom shading gradient like a drum. When its digit changes from old to new: jump (no animation) to index old, set a blur of size × 0.06, and animate index to 30 + new with .timingCurve(0.3, 0, 0.2, 1.08) over 0.9 s + 0.25 s × reel order, so reels land left to right with a small overshoot; ease the blur off over the last 30 %, and on completion jump back to index new without animation. With Reduce Motion on, animate straight to the new digit in 0.3 s.
effects.summary: Number reels spin with motion blur and land one after another.

effects.name: Price Ticker
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI PriceTicker(value:fractionDigits:prefix:) view (iOS 17+): an HStack of a 10 pt "arrowtriangle.up.fill" / "arrowtriangle.down.fill" (hidden when flat) and the prefix + value formatted with fractionDigits decimals, monospacedDigit, with .contentTransition(.numericText(value:)) and .snappy(0.35 s) animation so digits roll. On change, record the direction (green up, red down) for the arrow and text colour, and bump a counter that drives keyframeAnimator on a rounded background in that colour: opacity 0 → 0.3 (0.05 s) → 0 (0.9 s), a quick flash. With Reduce Motion on, skip the roll animation and the flash.
effects.summary: Digits roll to the new price as the background flashes green or red.

effects.name: Animated Chart
effects.prompt: Create two SwiftUI chart views without Swift Charts (iOS 17+). GrowingBarChart(values:color:spacing:): in a GeometryReader, an HStack(alignment: .bottom) of bars with top-rounded UnevenRoundedRectangles filled with the colour's gradient, bar width = width / (n + (n − 1) × spacing) with spacing 0.35; heights are 0 until onAppear sets grown, then height × value / max with .spring(duration: 0.6, bounce: 0.3) delayed 0.06 s × index, and springing to new heights when values change. DrawingLineChart(values:color:duration:): map values into the rect (5–6 pt inset), smooth with midpoint quadratic curves, stroke it 3 pt with round caps trimmed to progress, fill the closed area under it with a colour 35 % → clear gradient at opacity progress, and pop a 9 pt dot with a white ring onto the last point with a bouncy spring once progress reaches 1. In .task(id: values), reset progress to 0 without animation and animate to 1 with .easeInOut(1.2 s). With Reduce Motion on, use short eases.
effects.summary: Bars grow up one after another; a line draws itself left to right.

effects.name: Needle Gauge
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI NeedleGauge(value:colors:label:) view (iOS 17+), value 0…1, square. Draw a 240° arc (from 150° to 30° clockwise, radius 42 % of the side, line width 8 %, round caps): a secondary-15 % track, and on top an animatable arc Shape trimmed to the value and stroked with an AngularGradient of green, yellow, red over the same angles. Add 11 tick capsules (longer every fifth) rotated from −120° to +120°, a primary-coloured needle capsule rotated −120° + 240° × value, and a hub circle. Animate the needle with .spring(duration: 0.9, bounce: 0.45) so it overshoots and settles. Below the hub, show the label or the percentage with .contentTransition(.numericText). With Reduce Motion on, use a 0.3 s ease.
effects.summary: A speedometer needle swings to the value, overshoots and settles.

effects.name: Particle Field
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI ParticleField view (iOS 17+) with count (50), color, speed (14 pt/s) and linkDistance (70 pt). Generate each particle's traits once from a seeded SplitMix64 generator: start position (0…1 in each axis), direction, speed factor (0.4–1.2), radius (1–2.8 pt) and opacity (0.4–1). In TimelineView(.animation) with a Canvas, compute each position as start + direction × time × speed × factor, wrapped around the canvas edges, so there is no stored state. Stroke a 0.8 pt line between every pair closer than linkDistance with opacity 0.35 × (1 − distance / linkDistance), then fill each particle as a circle. Hide it from accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, freeze time.
effects.summary: Drifting particles linked by faint lines, like a living constellation.

effects.name: Starfield
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI Starfield view (iOS 17+) with count (200), speed (0.35 depth units per second) and color. Give each star a seeded random x and y in −1…1 and a depth in 0…1. In a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), compute z = 0.05 + 0.95 × fract(depth − time × speed), so stars approach the camera and wrap back to the far plane. Project with perspective: point = centre + (x, y) / z × 0.15 × half the larger side. Draw each star as a round-capped streak from its projection at a slightly larger z (z + min(0.08, speed × 0.05)) to its current projection, with opacity and line width growing as it gets closer. Hide it from accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, freeze time.
effects.summary: Stars stream out of the centre and stretch into streaks: warp speed.

effects.name: Cover Flow
effects.prompt: Create a generic SwiftUI CoverFlow carousel (iOS 17+) over Identifiable items with an optional selection binding, itemWidth (140), spacing (−10) and maxAngle (50°). Use a horizontal ScrollView + LazyHStack with .scrollTargetLayout(), .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned), hidden indicators, .scrollPosition(id:anchor: .center) and contentMargins that centre the first and last items. In .visualEffect, read the item's frame in the .scrollView coordinate space, compute p = clamp((midX − viewport centre) / itemWidth, −1, 1) and apply rotation3DEffect of −p × maxAngle around the y axis (perspective 0.6), scale 1 − |p| × 0.18 and brightness −|p| × 0.25. Raise the selected item's zIndex. With Reduce Motion on, drop the rotation.
effects.summary: Side items turn away in 3D, shrink and dim; the centre faces you.

effects.name: Float 3D
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .float3D(height:angle:period:shadow:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Inside TimelineView(.animation), let t = time × 2π / period (3 s) and lift = 0.5 + 0.5·sin t. Rotate the content in 3D by sin(t/2) × angle (12°) around the y axis and cos(0.7t) × angle/2 around the x axis (perspective 0.5), and move it up by height (10 pt) × lift. Behind it, at the bottom, draw a black ellipse 12 pt tall, 18 pt below, that gets lighter (opacity 0.25 − 0.1·lift), narrower (scale x 0.75 − 0.15·lift) and blurrier (6 + 4·lift) as the view rises. With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline.
effects.summary: The view hovers: a gentle bob, a slow 3D sway and a breathing shadow.
effects.usage:
Image("product")
    .resizable()
    .scaledToFit()
    .frame(width: 180)
    .float3D()

BadgeView()
    .float3D(height: 6, angle: 8, period: 4, shadow: false)

effects.name: Fireworks
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI Fireworks view (iOS 17+) with colors, interval (0.9 s between launches) and sparks (36 per burst), drawn statelessly in a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Rocket k launches at k × interval; for every rocket younger than 0.8 s climb + 1.5 s fade, seed a SplitMix64 generator with k to pick x (15–85 % of the width), peak height (15–45 %), colour and reach (22–34 % of the smaller side). Climbing: ease-out from the bottom to the peak and draw a 14 pt trail. Bursting, with t = time since the burst / 1.5: place each spark at angle i / sparks × 2π (plus jitter), distance reach × (1 − (1 − min(1, 1.6 t))³) × random 0.75–1, add gravity fall t² × 0.6 × reach, draw a circle of radius 1.8 × (1 − 0.6 t) at opacity 1 − t, and add a white flash for the first 15 %. Hide from accessibility; with Reduce Motion on, freeze on a frame with a burst in bloom.
effects.summary: Rockets climb and burst into rings of falling, fading sparks.

effects.name: Snowfall & Rain
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI Snowfall view (iOS 17+) with a style (.snow or .rain), count (80), color and speed. Give each particle seeded random traits: start x and y (0–1), depth (0–1) and phase. In a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), compute positions as pure functions of time, wrapped around the view so nothing is stored. Snow: fall speed 18 + 30 × depth pt/s, horizontal sway sin(time × (0.8 + depth) + phase) × (6 + 10 × depth) plus a slow 4 pt/s drift, radius 1 + 2.4 × depth, opacity 0.35 + 0.6 × depth, so small flakes look far away. Rain: fall speed 380 + 320 × depth, a streak 8 + 14 × depth long slanted by 0.25, width 0.8 + 0.8 × depth, opacity 0.25 + 0.5 × depth. Hide from accessibility; Reduce Motion pauses it.
effects.summary: Drifting, swaying snowflakes or fast slanted rain, with depth.

effects.name: Floating Reactions
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .floatingReactions(trigger:emojis:height:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Every time trigger changes, append a reaction (UUID, a random emoji from the list, a random sway of ±8–18 pt and drift of ±20 pt) to a @State array and remove it 2.3 s later. In a bottom-aligned, hit-testing-disabled overlay, show each emoji (28 pt) with keyframeAnimator(initialValue:trigger:), triggered by a @State flag set in onAppear so it plays once, over {y, x, scale, opacity}: y goes to −height (160 pt) over 2.2 s; x weaves sway → −sway + drift → sway + drift → drift in four 0.55 s cubic keyframes; scale springs from 0.3 to 1.15 and settles at 1; opacity holds for 1.4 s then fades over 0.8 s. With Reduce Motion on, don't spawn reactions.
effects.summary: Live-stream style emoji float up, swaying, every time you react.

effects.name: Warp Tunnel
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI WarpTunnel view (iOS 17+) with rings (18), colors (cyan, blue, purple, pink), speed (1.2 rings per second) and sides (0 for circles, 3+ for polygons). In a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), for ring i let depth = 1 − (i + fract(time × speed)) / rings and skip depths below 0.02. Its radius is half the view's diagonal × 0.06 / depth (perspective), skipped once it's 1.5 × larger than that. Stroke a circle, or a polygon rotated by i × 0.12 + time × 0.1 rad, centred in the view, with opacity closeness² and line width 0.5 + 3 × closeness (closeness = 1 − depth), cycling colours by ring. Hide from accessibility; Reduce Motion pauses it.
effects.summary: Rings rush out of the vanishing point toward you: flying down a tunnel.

effects.name: Holographic Card
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .holographic(cornerRadius:maxAngle:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Track the pointer with .onContinuousHover and a finger with a simultaneous DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0), normalising the location to p in −1…1 on both axes (nil when released). Overlay, clipped to a continuous rounded rectangle: (1) a rainbow LinearGradient (red → … → purple → red) from (−0.5 + 0.6 px, −0.5 + 0.3 py) to (1.5 + 0.6 px, 1.5 + 0.3 py) with .blendMode(.overlay), at 55 % opacity while touched and 15 % at rest; (2) a white 70 % → clear RadialGradient centred at (0.5 + 0.5 px, 0.5 + 0.5 py) with .blendMode(.softLight), visible only while touched. Tilt with rotation3DEffect: −py × maxAngle (14°) around x and px × maxAngle around y, perspective 0.6, and scale to 1.03 while touched. Follow with .interactiveSpring(response: 0.25) and release with .spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.6). With Reduce Motion on, keep the foil and glare but don't tilt or scale.
effects.summary: A trading card that tilts toward you with a rainbow foil and moving glare.

effects.name: Physics Emoji
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI PhysicsEmoji(trigger:emojis:batch:size:) view (iOS 17+) with a tiny physics world in a plain reference type stepped from a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Each change of trigger drops batch (6) bodies of radius size / 2 (30 pt emoji) at random x above the top with small random velocities and spin; keep at most 36, removing the oldest. Each frame (dt capped at 1/30 s, two substeps): add gravity 1400 pt/s², integrate, bounce off the floor with restitution 0.45 (stopping tiny bounces below 30 pt/s), damp sideways speed by 0.9 and make spin follow rolling speed (vx / r), bounce off the side walls, then resolve circle–circle overlaps by pushing pairs apart along the normal and exchanging the normal impulse −(1 + e) × relative / 2. Decay spin by 0.97 per frame. Draw each emoji (resolved once per frame) translated and rotated. Disable hit testing and hide from accessibility. With Reduce Motion on, place new emoji directly on the floor without falling.
effects.summary: Emoji tumble in with gravity, bounce off each other and pile up.

effects.name: Shatter
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI ShatterTransition (iOS 17+, Transition) with a static .shatter accessor. Build shards in unit coordinates from a 4 × 3 grid whose interior points are jittered by ±30 % of a cell, splitting each cell into two triangles along alternating diagonals. Removal applies an Animatable ViewModifier with progress 0 → 1 that renders the plain content at 0 (so an intact view isn't drawn once per shard) and otherwise a ZStack of the content masked by each triangle Shape (with a 0.8 pt stroke bleed to hide seams), rotated around its centroid by (r − 0.5) × 220° × p, offset along the centre-to-centroid direction by 110 pt × (0.6 + 0.6r) × p horizontally and 0.6 × 110 × p plus a falling 0.9 × 110 × p² vertically, with opacity 1 − p². Insertion just scales up from 0.9 and fades in. Read Reduce Motion in an inner View (Transition structs can't hold @Environment) and then use distance and spin 0 so shards only fade.
effects.summary: The view breaks into triangular shards that fly, spin and fall away.

effects.name: 3D Cube
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI CubeTransition (iOS 17+, Transition) with .cube and .cube(edge:) accessors. Map the phase to a position: willAppear = +1 (waiting on the trailing side), identity = 0, didDisappear = −1 (flip the signs for edge .leading). Inside visualEffect (to read the view's width), apply offset(x: width × position) and rotation3DEffect(90° × position, axis y, anchor .leading when position > 0 else .trailing, perspective 0.5). Halfway through, the outgoing face's trailing edge and the incoming face's leading edge meet in the middle like two faces of a cube. Read Reduce Motion in an inner View and cross-fade instead.
effects.summary: Views swap by turning a cube: one face folds away as the next rotates in.

effects.name: Dot Globe
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI DotGlobe(dots:color:accent:speed:) view (iOS 17+), square, drawn in a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Place 700 points on a unit sphere with the Fibonacci method (y = 1 − 2(i + 0.5)/n, ring = √(1 − y²), θ = golden angle × i + time × 0.6), tilt them 0.35 rad around the x axis, and project orthographically onto a circle of radius 45 % of the side. With depth = (z + 1) / 2, draw each dot with radius (0.6 + 1.2 × depth) and opacity 0.12 + 0.88 × depth², so the back is faint. Every 61st dot is a "city" in the accent colour (on the front half) whose radius pulses with sin(time × 3 + i). Add a faint 15 % rim circle. With Reduce Motion on, don't rotate.
effects.summary: A globe of evenly spread dots spins on a tilted axis, with pulsing cities.

effects.name: Bubbles
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI Bubbles(count:color:speed:) view (iOS 17+) drawn in a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Each of 18 bubbles has a stable random radius (6–22 pt), rise time (4–8 s), phase and x; progress = ((time + phase) / duration) mod 1 moves it from below the bottom to above the top while x wobbles by 14 pt × sin(time × (1 + r) + i). Fade in over the first ~17 % and out over the last 20 %. Fill each with a radial gradient (2 % → 12 % → 35 % of the tint, transparent centre), stroke a 1 pt rim with a diagonal pink → tint → purple gradient, and add a small white oval highlight at the top-left. With Reduce Motion on, show one still frame.
effects.summary: Soap bubbles rise and wobble with rainbow rims and glossy highlights.

effects.name: Fireflies
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI Fireflies(count:color:speed:) view (iOS 17+) drawn in a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Each firefly has three stable random values a, b, c; its position is the view centre plus two layered sines per axis (x: 0.38 sin(t(0.13 + 0.12a) + 20a) + 0.1 sin(t(0.5 + 0.3b) + 9b); y: 0.36 sin(t(0.11 + 0.1b) + 17b) + 0.1 cos(t(0.45 + 0.3c) + 5c), as fractions of the size), giving slow wandering loops. Its blink = (0.5 + 0.5 sin(t(0.8 + 1.6c) + 30a))³. Draw a glow circle 8 × r wide in a context with .blur(radius: 6) at opacity 0.25 + 0.75 × blink, then a white core of radius r (1.6–2.8 pt) at 0.35 + 0.65 × blink. Warm yellow by default. With Reduce Motion on, freeze positions but keep the blinking.
effects.summary: Glowing fireflies drift lazily and blink on their own rhythms.

effects.name: Iris
effects.prompt: Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+, the Transition protocol) called IrisTransition with an origin UnitPoint (centre), exposed as .iris and .iris(origin:). In body(content:phase:), mask the content with a GeometryReader containing a Circle whose radius is the distance from the origin point to the furthest corner, positioned at the origin, with scaleEffect(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: origin). The circle grows from the origin to cover the view on insertion and closes back on removal, timed by whatever animation drives the change, e.g. withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.6)). It only masks, so it needs no Reduce Motion fallback.
effects.summary: A circle opens from a point to reveal the view, like a camera iris.

effects.name: Blinds
effects.prompt: Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called BlindsTransition with a slats count (8), exposed as .blinds and .blinds(slats:). In body(content:phase:), mask the content with a VStack(spacing: 0) of slats Rectangles, each with scaleEffect(y: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: .top), so every slat grows down from its top edge at the same time on insertion and folds back up on removal. It only masks, so it needs no Reduce Motion fallback.
effects.summary: Horizontal slats open together to reveal the view, like Venetian blinds.

effects.name: Clock Wipe
effects.prompt: Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called ClockWipeTransition, exposed as .clockWipe. Mask the content with an animatable Shape whose animatableData is progress (0…1): it returns the full rect at 1, an empty path at 0, and otherwise a pie wedge from the centre with radius equal to the rect's diagonal, from −90° to −90° + 360° × progress (clockwise: false, which sweeps clockwise on screen in SwiftUI's y-down space). Pass progress 1 when phase.isIdentity and 0 otherwise, so the animation interpolates the angle. It only masks, so it needs no Reduce Motion fallback.
effects.summary: A wedge sweeps clockwise from twelve o'clock, like a clock hand.

effects.name: Pixel Dissolve
effects.prompt: Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called DissolveTransition with a cellSize (10 pt), exposed as .dissolve and .dissolve(cellSize:). Mask the content with an animatable Shape whose animatableData is progress (0…1): divide the rect into a grid of cellSize squares, give each cell a stable pseudo-random threshold in 0…1 from an integer hash of (column, row), and add the cells whose threshold is below progress (outset by 0.25 pt so neighbours don't leave seams); return the full rect at 1 and an empty path at 0. Pass progress 1 when phase.isIdentity and 0 otherwise. It only masks, so it needs no Reduce Motion fallback.
effects.summary: The view appears and vanishes in square pixels, in random order.

effects.name: Poof
effects.prompt: Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called PoofTransition, exposed as .poof. Return a small view that reads Reduce Motion and applies: scale 1.35 when phase == .didDisappear, 0.7 when .willAppear, 1 at identity; blur radius 14 when not identity, 0 at identity; opacity 0 when not identity. Removal swells and blurs away like smoke, insertion condenses in from a smaller blur. With Reduce Motion on, keep the scale at 1 (blur and fade only).
effects.summary: The view puffs away like smoke: it swells and blurs out.

effects.name: Swoosh
effects.prompt: Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called SwooshTransition, exposed as .swoosh. Use phase.value (−1 before insertion, 0 at rest, +1 after removal) as v and apply a GeometryEffect whose animatableData is v: a CGAffineTransform with c = −0.6 v (a horizontal skew) and tx = v × width − c × height / 2 (slide by the view's own width, skewing around the vertical centre). Add blur 6 × |v| and opacity 1 − |v|, so it whooshes in from the leading edge leaning into the motion and leaves to the trailing edge. With Reduce Motion on, skip the slide and skew (fade only).
effects.summary: The view whooshes in leaning forward, with a motion blur.

effects.name: Film Exposure
effects.prompt: Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called FilmExposureTransition, exposed as .filmExposure. When the phase isn't identity, apply brightness 0.9, saturation 0 and opacity 0; at identity, brightness 0, saturation 1 and opacity 1. Inserting the view develops it like a photo, from blown-out colourless white to full colour, and removing it fades it back out to white. Nothing moves, so it needs no Reduce Motion fallback.
effects.summary: The view develops like a photo, from over-exposed white to full colour.

effects.name: Circular Reveal
effects.prompt: Create a generic SwiftUI CircularReveal(value:origin:duration:content:) view (iOS 17+) where origin is a UnitPoint. Keep @State shown (initially value), incoming (optional) and progress. When value changes: if a reveal is in flight, commit it; set incoming = new and progress = 0 without animation, then animate progress to 1 with .easeInOut(0.7 s) and, on completion, set shown = new and incoming = nil without animation. Render ZStack { content(shown); content(incoming) masked by an animatable circle Shape centred at origin whose radius is progress × the distance to the furthest corner }, with hit testing off on the incoming layer. To start at a tap, convert the location with UnitPoint(x: x / width, y: y / height). With Reduce Motion on, cross-fade the incoming layer instead of growing the circle.
effects.summary: New content spreads out in a circle from where you tapped.

effects.name: Liquid Swipe
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI LiquidSwipeTransition (iOS 17+, Transition) with a .liquidSwipe accessor. Mask the content with an animatable Shape whose progress is 0 on willAppear and 1 otherwise: at progress p it covers the view from the trailing edge to edge = maxX − (width + a) × p, where the bulge a = 0.35 × width × sin(πp); the leading boundary is straight except for a wave from midY − 0.45h to midY + 0.45h drawn with two cubic curves that bulge out to edge − a at midY. Darken the outgoing view with brightness −0.15 and give the incoming view zIndex 1 so it draws on top. Read Reduce Motion in an inner View and use no bulge.
effects.summary: The next page pours in from the edge behind a bulging liquid wave.

effects.name: Page Turn
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI PageTurnTransition (iOS 17+, Transition) with a .pageTurn accessor. The outgoing view gets zIndex 1 and an Animatable ViewModifier with progress 0 → 1: rotation3DEffect(−90° × p, axis y, anchor .leading, perspective 0.6), an overlay LinearGradient from clear to black at 45 % × p (leading → trailing) so the free edge darkens as it turns, a shadow of opacity 0.3 × sin(πp), radius 12, x 6, and opacity 0 at the very end. The incoming view sits underneath and brightens from −0.25 to 0. Read Reduce Motion in an inner View and simply fade the page out.
effects.summary: The old page swings away like a book page, revealing the next one.

effects.name: Glitch Transition
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI GlitchTransition (iOS 17+, Transition) with .glitch and .glitch(slices:) accessors that applies an Animatable ViewModifier with amount 0 (identity) → 1 (inserted or removed). At 0 render the content as is. Otherwise, with frame = Int(amount × 16) so the pattern changes in steps: stack a red copy (colorMultiply(.red), offset x −amount × 10, 60 %), a cyan copy (offset +amount × 10, 60 %) and 7 horizontal slices of the content, each masked to its band and offset sideways by (random(slice, frame) − 0.5) × 60 × amount; composite them and set opacity to 1 − 0.6 × amount, or 0.15 when random(frame) ≤ 0.9 × amount, reaching 0 at the end. Read Reduce Motion in an inner View and fade instead.
effects.summary: The view breaks up like a bad signal on its way in or out.

effects.name: Origami Fold
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI OrigamiTransition (iOS 17+, Transition) with .origami and .origami(folds:) accessors applying an Animatable ViewModifier with progress 0 (flat) → 1 (folded). At 0 render the content. Otherwise keep the footprint with content.hidden() and, in a top-aligned overlay GeometryReader, draw 4 copies of the content, each masked to its horizontal panel. With angle = 90° × p and c = cos(angle): even panels hinge on their top edge (rotation3DEffect +angle about x, anchor at y = i / n), odd panels on their bottom edge (−angle, anchor (i + 1) / n), and each is offset by hinge × panelHeight × (c − 1) so it starts where the previous one ends, collapsing like an accordion towards the top. Shade panels with black at (0.1 even, 0.4 odd) × (1 − c), perspective 0.4, and fade out over the last 15 %. Read Reduce Motion in an inner View and fade instead.
effects.summary: The view folds up into creased panels like a paper map.

effects.name: Water Ripple
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .waterRipple(at:trigger:amplitude:duration:) view modifier (iOS 17+) using a Metal [[stitchable]] layer shader. The shader takes (float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float2 origin, float time, float amplitude, float frequency, float decay, float speed): distance = length(position − origin), local = max(0, time − distance / speed), wave = amplitude × sin(frequency × local) × exp(−decay × local); sample the layer at position + wave × normalize(position − origin) and add 0.25 × wave / amplitude to rgb (times alpha) so crests brighten. In Swift, run keyframeAnimator(initialValue: 0, trigger:) with MoveKeyframe(0) and a LinearKeyframe to duration (3 s) over duration, and apply .visualEffect { $0.layerEffect(ShaderLibrary.motionRipple(.float2(origin), .float(elapsed), .float(12), .float(15), .float(8), .float(1200)), maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: 12, height: 12), isEnabled: 0 < elapsed < duration) }. Add .waterRippleOnTap() that records a SpatialTapGesture location (as a simultaneous gesture) and bumps the trigger. With Reduce Motion on, disable the effect.
effects.summary: A real ripple distorts the view's pixels outward from a tap.
effects.usage:
import MotionShaders

Image("pond")
    .waterRippleOnTap()

Card()
    .waterRipple(at: tapLocation, trigger: tapCount)

effects.name: Pixellate
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .pixellate(_ size:) view modifier (iOS 17+) as an Animatable ViewModifier over size, so withAnimation interpolates the block size. It applies .layerEffect(ShaderLibrary.motionPixellate(.float(size)), maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: size, height: size), isEnabled: size > 1). The Metal [[stitchable]] shader (float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float size) returns layer.sample(position) when size ≤ 1, otherwise layer.sample((floor(position / size) + 0.5) × size), one colour per block.
effects.summary: The view melts into a mosaic of square blocks and back.

effects.name: Chromatic Aberration
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .chromaticAberration(_ amount:) view modifier (iOS 17+) as an Animatable ViewModifier over amount, applying .layerEffect(ShaderLibrary.motionChromatic(.float(amount)), maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: |amount|, height: 0), isEnabled: |amount| > 0.01). The Metal [[stitchable]] shader (float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float amount) samples red at position + (amount, 0), green at position and blue at position − (amount, 0), with alpha = the max of the three samples' alpha. For a beat, spike amount to 7 pt with withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.12)) and, in its completion, ease back to 1.5 over 0.5 s.
effects.summary: Red and blue split sideways like a cheap lens; animate it on a beat.

effects.name: CRT Screen
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .crtScreen(curvature:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Inside TimelineView(.animation), apply .visualEffect { $0.layerEffect(ShaderLibrary.motionCRT(.float2(proxy.size), .float(time), .float(curvature)), maxSampleOffset: size × curvature) } with curvature 0.06. The Metal [[stitchable]] shader (position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float2 size, float time, float curvature): map to centred uv in −1…1, barrel-distort with uv × (1 + curvature × dot(uv, uv)), return black outside 0…1; sample red at +0.8 pt and blue at −0.8 pt for fringing; multiply by scanlines 0.8 + 0.2 sin(y × π × 0.66), a rolling band 1 + 0.08 × smoothstep(0.92, 1, sin(uv.y × 3 − time × 1.5)), a vignette smoothstep(1.25, 0.4, length(centred)) and a flicker 0.97 + 0.03 sin(time × 60). With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline at time 0.
effects.summary: Curved glass, scanlines, a rolling band and flicker, like an old monitor.

effects.name: Heat Haze
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .heatHaze(strength:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Inside TimelineView(.animation), apply .visualEffect { $0.distortionEffect(ShaderLibrary.motionHeatHaze(.float2(proxy.size), .float(time), .float(strength)), maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: strength, height: strength)) } with strength 6 pt. The Metal [[stitchable]] distortion shader (float2 position, float2 size, float time, float strength) uses smooth value noise: rise = y × 0.05 + time × 2, n = noise(x × 0.04, rise) − 0.5, m = noise(x × 0.09 + 10, rise × 1.7) − 0.5, weight = 0.35 + 0.65 × y / height (stronger at the bottom), and returns position + ((n + 0.5m) × strength × weight, n × strength × 0.3 × weight). With Reduce Motion on, use strength 0.
effects.summary: The view shimmers like hot air over a desert road.

effects.name: Noise Dissolve
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .noiseDissolve(_ progress:scale:edge:) view modifier (iOS 17+) as an Animatable ViewModifier over progress, applying .colorEffect(ShaderLibrary.motionDissolve(.float(progress), .float(scale), .color(edge)), isEnabled: progress > 0) with scale 18 pt and an orange edge, plus a NoiseDissolveTransition (.noiseDissolve) that uses progress 1 when not identity. The Metal [[stitchable]] colour shader (float2 position, half4 color, float progress, float scale, half4 edge): n = 0.7 × noise(position / scale) + 0.3 × noise(position / (0.35 × scale)) using smooth value noise; threshold = progress × 1.1 − 0.05; return transparent where n < threshold, and mix towards edge × alpha by 1 − smoothstep(threshold, threshold + 0.06, n) so a thin band glows just before it burns. With Reduce Motion on, the transition fades instead.
effects.summary: The view burns away in organic blotches with a glowing edge.
effects.usage:
import MotionShaders

Card()
    .noiseDissolve(isDeleting ? 1 : 0)
    .animation(.easeIn(duration: 1), value: isDeleting)

if !isDeleted {
    NoteCard().transition(.noiseDissolve)
}

install:
```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library", branch: "main")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "MotionLibrary", package: "SwiftUI-Motion-Library")
```

Then `import MotionLibrary`. Requires iOS 17, macOS 14 or visionOS 1; effects marked iOS 18+ are `@available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)`.
